statement: Recalibrated AMS radiocarbon chronology places the end of Mousterian (Neanderthal-associated) archaeological assemblages at 41,030-39,260 calibrated years before present (95.4% probability) across the sampled European range — revising downward earlier claims of Neanderthal survival to as recently as ~24,000 years ago at some sites (e.g. Gorham’s Cave, Gibraltar), which this study attributes largely to contamination in older, unfiltered radiocarbon samples.

sources.citation: Higham, T. et al. "The timing and spatiotemporal patterning of Neanderthal disappearance." Nature 512: 306-309.
sources.author: Higham et al.

notes: Some subsequent work (e.g. on Northwest Europe) argues for regional refinements, but the ~40,000-year figure (not the older ~24,000-year claims) is the current mainstream consensus figure.
